claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct enforced entirely within Pulumi.
The Pulumi `protect` resource option is never sent to the cloud provider.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is a deletion-protection setting separate from Pulumi's `protect` option.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is a deletion-protection setting separate from Pulumi's `protect` option.
Cloud provider deletion-protection attributes (such as `deletionProtection`) are enforced by the cloud provider independently of anything Pulumi knows about.
A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi and still refuse to delete because of provider-side deletion protection, or be protected in Pulumi and yet be deletable at the provider level.

The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi protect and provider deletion protection apart and resolve each.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes that the cloud provider or cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi's `protect` resource option.
GCP Cloud SQL instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute (deletion protection enforced by the provider or cloud API).
AWS RDS instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute (deletion protection enforced by the provider or cloud API).
Pulumi's `protect` resource option and a resource's own provider/cloud-level deletion-protection attributes are complementary rather than substitutes for one another.

The Pulumi docs page 'destroy-failures' has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi's protect and resource-level deletion protection apart and how to resolve a destroy failure caused by either.

Deletion protection that causes a `pulumi destroy` failure can be held at three distinct layers (Pulumi's `protect` option, a provider-enforced flag, a cloud-API-enforced protection), and the error message usually indicates which one was hit.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
When `pulumi destroy` fails because of the `protect` resource option, the error names a URN and mentions `protect`.
The page /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ exists and explains how to remove the `protect` option.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, e.g. `deletionProtection` on `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` or `gcp.container.Cluster`.
For provider-enforced deletion protection, the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
Some clouds reject the delete call themselves independent of Pulumi, e.g. AWS RDS `deletionProtection`, EC2 `disableApiTermination`, or an Azure Resource Manager management lock.
For cloud-API-enforced protection, the error text comes back from the cloud provider's API, often with a distinct error code such as `ScopeLocked` (Azure management lock).
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is already recorded in the stack's state, not what the program currently says, so setting the attribute to `false` in the program alone is not enough.

Remediation for provider-enforced and cloud-API-enforced deletion protection: set the attribute to `false` in the program, run `pulumi up` so the change reaches both the live resource and Pulumi's state, then run `pulumi destroy`.

If deletion protection was already disabled outside Pulumi (e.g., in the cloud console), `pulumi refresh` synchronizes the stack's state with reality and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.container.Cluster` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
Destroying a `gcp.bigquery.Dataset` that still contains tables fails unless `deleteContentsOnDestroy` is `true`.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute enforced by the AWS API that defaults to `false`.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` `forceDestroy` defaults to `false`, and a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
`aws.ec2.Instance` has a `disableApiTermination` attribute enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
`aws.dynamodb.Table` has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute enforced by the AWS API that defaults to `false`.
`azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel` exist in the azure-native provider.
An Azure management lock of type `CanNotDelete` is enforced by Azure Resource Manager and must be removed before the resource can be deleted, independent of the Pulumi program.
Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it.
Recreating an Azure Key Vault with the same name fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered.
Azure Key Vault purge protection prevents purging the soft-deleted vault until its retention period elapses.
